concept.body: Both angles are measured from a horizontal line at the observer's eye: elevation opens upward, depression opens downward. Because the observer's horizontal is parallel to the ground, a depression angle at the top equals the elevation angle at the bottom (alternate interior angles) — so you can always relocate it inside the triangle.

explanationVariants: Alternate interior angles between parallel horizontals: the elevation at the ground equals the 40° depression.
Depression from tower to car = elevation from car to tower: 40°.

widget.prompt: The angle of depression from a tower to a car is 40°. The angle of elevation from the car to the tower top = ? (degrees)

commonErrors.feedback: 50 = 90 − 40 is the complement, the angle at the tower's TOP corner inside the triangle. The relocated angle equals 40°.
140 = 180 − 40 is a supplement along a straight line — not this setup. Parallels + transversal: equal, 40°.

steps.body: Look UP at a treetop: the angle between the **horizontal** and your line of sight is the **angle of elevation**. Look DOWN from a cliff at a boat: the angle below the horizontal is the **angle of depression**. Both are measured from the horizontal — never from the vertical, and never from the slope itself.

widget.prompt: An observer on a cliff looks down at a boat. The angle of depression is measured between which two lines?

options.label: The horizontal line at the observer's eye, and the line of sight down to the boat
options.feedback: Depression always opens DOWNWARD from the observer's horizontal to the line of sight.

options.label: The cliff face and the line of sight
options.feedback: The cliff face is VERTICAL — measuring from it gives the complement, 90° minus the true angle. Start from the horizontal.

options.label: The sea surface and the cliff face
options.feedback: Those two lines meet at the cliff's base, away from the observer. Depression lives at the observer's eye, below their horizontal.

options.label: The line of sight and the vertical drop to the boat
options.feedback: That's the angle at the BOAT's side of the triangle rearranged — from the observer, measure horizontal down to line of sight.

steps.body: The elevation-depression triangle almost always has the same three parts: a **height** (vertical leg), a **horizontal distance** (horizontal leg), and the **line of sight** (hypotenuse). Height and horizontal distance are the two legs — so **tangent** does most of the work in these problems.

explanationVariants: The height is opposite the 32° angle; 50 m is adjacent. tan 32° = h/50 → h = 50·tan 32° ≈ 31.24 m.
Two legs (height and ground distance) → tangent: 50·tan 32° ≈ 31.24 m.

widget.prompt: From 50 m away (on flat ground), the angle of elevation to a treetop is 32°. How high is the treetop above eye level, in meters (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 26.5 = 50·sin 32° treats the 50 m GROUND distance as the line of sight. It's the adjacent leg: 50·tan 32° ≈ 31.24.
80.02 = 50 ÷ tan 32° divides — but the unknown height sits on TOP of tan 32° = h/50. Multiply: ≈ 31.24.
42.4 = 50·cos 32° mixes in cosine — yet no hypotenuse is known or wanted. Leg-to-leg is tangent: ≈ 31.24.

explanationVariants: tan 25° = h/60 → h = 60·tan 25° ≈ 27.98 m — a shallower angle, so less height per meter of distance.
Same tangent setup with the new numbers: 60 × 0.4663 ≈ 27.98 m.

widget.prompt: From 60 m away, the angle of elevation to a rooftop is 25°. Height above eye level, in meters (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 25.36 = 60·sin 25° casts the 60 m ground distance as the line of sight — it's the adjacent LEG. 60·tan 25° ≈ 27.98.
128.67 = 60 ÷ tan 25° divides — but the unknown height rides on TOP of tan 25° = h/60. Multiply: ≈ 27.98.
54.38 = 60·cos 25° brings in cosine with no hypotenuse in sight. Leg-to-leg is tangent: ≈ 27.98.

steps.body: Here's the gift: the observer's horizontal and the ground are **parallel lines**, and the line of sight is a transversal. So the angle of depression at the top equals the angle of elevation at the bottom — **alternate interior angles**. You may relocate a depression angle INSIDE the triangle at the far vertex, for free.

explanationVariants: The horizontal at the top and the ground are parallel; the line of sight crosses both, so the alternate interior angles are equal: also 15°.
Depression from A to B always equals elevation from B to A — 15°.

widget.prompt: From a cliff top, the angle of depression to a boat is 15°. What is the angle of ELEVATION from the boat up to the cliff top?

options.label: 15° — alternate interior angles between parallels
options.feedback: The two horizontals are parallel; the line of sight is a transversal, so the angles match exactly.

options.label: 75° — the complement
options.feedback: 75° = 90 − 15 is the angle the sight line makes with the VERTICAL cliff, not with the boat's horizontal. Elevation = 15°.

options.label: 165° — the supplement
options.feedback: 165° = 180 − 15 pairs angles along a straight line — the wrong relationship. Parallels + transversal give equal angles: 15°.

options.label: It depends on the cliff's height
options.feedback: Height changes the DISTANCES, never this angle equality — parallel horizontals force elevation = depression at any size.

widget.prompt: A drone hovers 120 m up; the angle of depression to the pad is 27°. Drag to 27° and read opp/adj — the ratio that links the height to the ground distance.
widget.successFeedback: tan 27° ≈ 0.51, so the ground distance is 120 ÷ 0.51 ≈ 235 m. Depression from the drone equals elevation from the pad — alternate angles across parallel horizontals — which is why one angle serves both viewpoints.
widget.lowFeedback: Under 27° — opp/adj is reading too small.
widget.highFeedback: Over 27° — opp/adj is reading too large.
widget.scaleFeedback: Resize the triangle before checking; the tangent of 27° is fixed by the angle alone.

hints: Relocate the 15° depression to the boat as a 15° elevation — alternate interior angles.
At the boat: opposite = the 80 m cliff, adjacent = the horizontal distance x. tan 15° = 80/x.
The unknown is on the bottom: x = 80 ÷ tan 15°.
explanationVariants: Moving 15° inside the triangle at the boat: x = 80 ÷ tan 15° ≈ 298.56 m.

widget.prompt: From the top of an 80 m cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 15°. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff, in meters (2 decimals)?

commonErrors.feedback: 21.44 = 80·tan 15° multiplies — but x sits on the BOTTOM of tan 15° = 80/x. Divide: 80 ÷ tan 15° ≈ 298.56.
309.1 = 80 ÷ sin 15° is the LINE-OF-SIGHT distance (hypotenuse) — real, but the question asks the horizontal leg: ≈ 298.56.
20.71 = 80·sin 15° treats 80 as the hypotenuse — the cliff is the vertical LEG. x = 80 ÷ tan 15° ≈ 298.56.

takeaways: Elevation looks up, depression looks down — both from the HORIZONTAL, never the vertical.
Depression from A to B = elevation from B to A (alternate interior angles).
Height + horizontal distance are legs, so tangent usually runs the show.
steps.teaser: Next: height problems — measure buildings, kites, and airplanes without leaving the ground.
